newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt convicts nine for police killing.
newsitem.headline: Egypt convicts nine for police killing.

text.p: An Egyptian state security court on Thursday sentenced nine Moslem militants to jail terms ranging from five years to life imprisonment for killing a senior police officer and his two assistants in southern Egypt in 1993.
The same court last month sentenced in absentia another two militants to death for the same charge. The judge acquitted seven others on Thursday because of lack of evidence.

The 18 militants stood trial for the killing of Major General Mohammed Abdel-Latif el-Gobashi, assistant security chief for the southern province of Qena, as he was leaving his house in Nag Hammadi, some 450 km (280 miles) south of Cairo.
The militants were also charged with shooting dead Gobashi's guard and driver, policemen Mohammed Sayyed and Nasser Mahmoud.
The court sentenced three of the militants to life imprisonment with hard labour, three to 15 years, one man to five years and two juvenile defendants, below 18, to 10 and seven years respectively.
One of the men sentenced to life imprisonment is a fugitive so is the one given a five-year jail term.

The prosecution said the men were members of al-Gama'a al-Islamiya (Islamic Group), the country's largest militant organisation. The group has been fighting since 1992 to overthrow the Egyptian government and set up a strict Islamic state.
The Gama'a has targeted policemen and senior officials but has also attacked Christians and tourists. More than 1,000 people have been killed in the political violence.
